evals.prompt: I’m about to send a photo of my friend and their LinkedIn URL. Can you import them as a Codex pet inspired by Mini Kenji, with a quiet coffee-thinking loop and a focused design-review pose? Before I send them, tell me what you’ll save from the research, how the animations fit the pet states, and what has to pass before installation.
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied image as likeness anchor; performs bounded public research; records sources and separates facts from inference; maps ideas into existing states; preserves the nine-row atlas; runs deterministic and visual QA before packaging
assertions: Uses the supplied image as the primary likeness anchor
Limits research to public pet-relevant cues and records sources
Separates public facts, user direction, inference, and unknowns
Maps animation ideas into the fixed nine Codex states
Preserves a style anchor without assuming local example pets exist
Requires deterministic and visual QA before packaging

farplane.title: Imports a friend from an image and bounded public profile research
anti_patterns: Builds a private dossier or infers sensitive traits
Lets profile text override the supplied likeness image
Adds custom atlas rows for personal animation ideas
Packages the pet without contact-sheet and motion QA

evals.prompt: I’m going to send a portrait and a public profile link that may not load. My note says they are a product designer who always carries a sketchbook. Will the broken profile block the pet, and how would that designer cue show up in the working and review animations?
evals.expected_output: Continues from the portrait and notes when the profile is inaccessible; records the limitation; does not invent facts; uses one readable sketchbook motif; maps work and review behavior into existing states
assertions: Does not block when image and user notes are sufficient
Records inaccessible-source limitations without inventing details
Uses a readable stable signature prop
Maps behavior into existing running and review state semantics

farplane.title: Falls back safely when a supplied public profile cannot be read
